docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: The terms these docs use, one per concept. Each links to the page that covers it.

docs.title: Images
docs.text: Term Meaning Component image A published container image holding one or more Autoware functions, for example planning. Latest alias An image tag such as planning-humble that follows the newest stable release. Release tags (-vX.Y.Z) and digests never move. Digest pin An image reference by content hash (@sha256:…) instead of a tag, so the same image bits are always used.

docs.title: Deployments
docs.text: Term Meaning Deployment A named, ready-to-run stack for one task, such as Planning Simulation: a deployment manifest, settings and Compose files. Deployment manifest deployment.json: what the CLI needs to run a deployment. Compose files, requirements, data downloads, one-shot services and the verify step. Settings KEY=value variables a deployment runs with, such as MAP_PATH: settings.env, then settings.gpu.env with --gpu, then the host settings file. run and restart apply them. Node One host's part of a split-host deployment, with its own services, Compose project, ROS domain and Zenoh endpoint.

docs.title: Kits
docs.text: Term Meaning Kit A kit manifest and its deployments: the reference kit in this repository, or your differences on top of a pinned release. Kit manifest openadkit.json: what the kit extends, its deployments (each named by its key) and the images it pins. extends / base The Open AD Kit release a kit pins, and the deployment of that release a kit deployment builds on. Config override Parameter and file differences under config/autoware/, merged over a package's configuration on every start; not a copy of the full file. restart applies them. Overlay workspace Your ROS packages in overlay_ws/, built in the release's devel image and sourced on top of Autoware.

docs.title: Releases and Evidence
docs.text: Term Meaning Evidence cell One runtime test of a deployment on one ROS distro and topology, such as planning-simulation-humble-linux-amd64. Evidence The evidence cells run against one build. A release needs a run in which every cell passed. CI exemption A reasoned manifest entry for a deployment without a hosted evidence cell. It is not a passing test. BOM A release's bill of materials: the pinned Autoware release, component images and external images.

docs.title: Platforms
docs.text: Term Meaning Mixed criticality Running safety-critical and non-critical workloads on separately qualified execution environments. Here, the Safety Island's real-time hardware beside the containerized stack; the containers on one host share its network and are not isolated by criticality.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: What Open AD Kit is, why it exists, and how it relates to Autoware.

docs.title: What is Open AD Kit
docs.text:
Open AD Kit packages the Autoware autonomous driving stack as focused, independently deployable container images. Instead of one monolithic image, it splits the stack along the AD pipeline (sensing and perception, localization and mapping, planning, control, vehicle and system, API, simulator and visualizer), so a deployment runs only what its task needs.

Autoware provides the autonomy stack; Open AD Kit makes it deployable. It packages upstream software into composable images, defines deployments, integrates target platforms, and maintains the build, test and release tooling that keeps a deployment the same from one host to the next. It ships simulation deployments today; a supported path to a real vehicle interface is on the roadmap.

It also integrates Autoware Safety Island, which runs on real-time operating systems and automotive hardware rather than in a container. Open AD Kit is the first SOAFEE blueprint for the software-defined vehicle; Supported Platforms covers the derived blueprints and the support tiers.

docs.title: Why Open AD Kit
docs.text:
Modular Components

Independent images for each stage of the AD pipeline. Deploy only what you need.

Mixed Criticality

Keep safety-critical control on the Safety Island's real-time hardware, beside the containerized stack.

Cloud Native

Scale from simulation to the edge with containerized deployments, reproducible image builds, and platform integrations.

Connected and Continuous

Every release promotes a CI build that passed its runtime evidence, with pinned image digests and build provenance.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
Open AD Kit runs Autoware as a pipeline of containers. Each container handles one stage of autonomous driving, and the stages talk over ROS 2 DDS on the host network.

  1. Sensing captures and preprocesses raw sensor data (LiDAR, camera, IMU).
  2. Perception detects and tracks objects, traffic lights, and drivable space.
  3. Mapping serves high-definition map data that the rest of the stack consumes.
  4. Localization determines the vehicle's exact position on the map.
  5. Planning computes a safe, feasible trajectory to the goal.
  6. Control converts that trajectory into throttle, brake, and steering commands.
  7. Vehicle & System bridges those commands to the vehicle or simulator and monitors the stack.

A deployment runs the subset of these stages a task needs. Autoware Safety Island joins the same pipeline over DDS, adding a safety-critical actuation path alongside the containerized services.

The Glossary defines the terms these docs use.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
Last reviewed: 2026-11-09, before v2.0.0.

What Open AD Kit plans next, as outcomes its users will notice. Finished work leaves this page and appears in the release notes. Maintenance and CI work is tracked in GitHub Issues, not here.

docs.title: Now: v2.0.0
docs.text: 1. The first stable release. A full build and evidence run, then a clean-host install, kit, restart and upgrade check on a release candidate.

docs.title: Next: v2.x, in priority order
docs.text:
1. Development tooling. A devcontainer and a debugging guide for the development loop.
  2. The base from a kit. Run a kit's unmodified base deployment from the kit, with the release it pins, to tell the kit's changes from the base.
  3. Two levels of base. A kit on a deployment that has a base itself, such as Safety Island Simulation.
  4. Comparable regression results. A fixed scenario set whose latency, resource use and driving metrics are compared with a baseline.
  5. Platform evidence. Native arm64 evidence cells, a readiness check and an evidence cell for Logging Simulation on CPU, and GPU logging simulation coverage.
  6. Image SBOMs. A software bill of materials for each container image.
  7. CES 2027 demo. Hardware integration and partner evidence for the demonstrated setup; tracked in #169.

docs.title: Later: direction, not commitment
docs.text:
• Autoware System Designer. It selects launch files and parameters; Open AD Kit selects images and Compose services. See Autoware System Designer.
  • Path to a vehicle. A vehicle-interface contract and reference hardware, a validation ladder from SIL to full-scale vehicles, and offline OCI delivery.
  • EWAOL. Decide whether the SOAFEE reference implementation, now kept by the SOAFEE SIG, becomes a target with a deployment validated on it, or leaves the support matrix.
  • Visualizer. KasmVNC in place of TigerVNC, noVNC and Openbox, at the next major version; Lichtblick with foxglove_bridge for analysis and bag playback.
  • rmw_zenoh. Replace zenoh-bridge-ros2dds for split-host on Jazzy if an evaluation succeeds.
  • Per-image trimming. Packages that no catalog deployment runs and that bring heavy dependencies, such as PyTorch for control's smart MPC, calibration tools and DNN packages in CPU images, in a minor release whose notes list them.
  • One layering mechanism. GPU modes, deployments on a base and split-host nodes each add differences to a stack by rules of their own; one mechanism could replace the three. It would come beside them in a minor release, and the old ones would go only at a major version.
  • Safety Island on CARLA. A kit with the Safety Island's closed loop over CAN, backed by its own runtime evidence.
  • Manifests without kind. extends already marks a kit and version a release, so kind repeats them. It could become optional in a minor release, with manifests that carry it still read.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text: No custom OTA service, Kubernetes stack, fork of upstream workloads, or ASIL or NCAP certification claim. Safety Island owns its safety boundary; Open AD Kit integrates it.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
Open AD Kit packages Autoware Universe into focused container images. Each image groups closely related Autoware functions, and deployments run them as separate containers that talk over ROS 2. External clients use the Autoware AD API; the images use Autoware's component interfaces between them.

All images build on a shared universe-common layer; see Build from Source for the build graph. The image reference lists tags and platforms.

The runtime images hold what Autoware runs. They leave out what only a compiler reads, such as headers and static libraries, and only the visualizer carries RViz and its plugins. A kit compiles its overlay workspace in the universe-common-devel image, which keeps both.

docs.title: Sensing & Perception
docs.text:
Sensor preprocessing and environment understanding in one image.

  • Sensing — LiDAR distortion correction, filtering, and point cloud preprocessing; camera and radar preprocessing; GNSS/INS preprocessing; shared point cloud container. Launch: component_sensing.launch.xml
  • Perception — camera, LiDAR, and radar object detection and fusion; multi-object tracking and trajectory prediction; traffic light recognition; occupancy grid mapping. Launch: component_perception.launch.xml
  • CUDA variant — sensing-perception-cuda accelerates point cloud processing and neural-network inference on NVIDIA GPUs. It is amd64-only and requires the NVIDIA Container Toolkit. Used by Logging Simulation (--gpu) and CARLA Simulation.

docs.title: Localization & Mapping
docs.text:
Serves HD maps and estimates the vehicle pose within them.

  • Localization — GNSS/RTK positioning and IMU dead reckoning; visual odometry and LiDAR map matching; automatic pose initialization; EKF state estimation. Launch: component_localization.launch.xml
  • Mapping — Lanelet2 vector map and point cloud map serving; occupancy grid and point cloud map construction; map coordinate transforms. Launch: component_map.launch.xml

Planning and Scenario Simulation run only the map service; the simulator supplies map-to-odometry transforms. Logging and CARLA Simulation also run localization.

docs.title: Planning
docs.text:
Trajectory generation: route planning on Lanelet2 road networks; behavior planning for lanes, intersections, and obstacles; kinematically feasible motion planning; goal and parking maneuvers; the planning validator that publishes /planning/trajectory. Launch: component_planning.launch.xml

  • CUDA variant — planning-cuda builds the same packages with CUDA and TensorRT, so planning_setting:=diffusion_planner runs Autoware 2.0's Diffusion Planner. It is amd64-only and requires the NVIDIA Container Toolkit. Used by Planning Simulation (--gpu).

docs.title: Control
docs.text: Vehicle control from /planning/trajectory: lateral steering and longitudinal velocity control; PID and Model Predictive Control modes; vehicle-specific command conversion; emergency stop and heartbeat monitoring. Control reads only that trajectory, so it stays the same whichever planner produces it. Launch: component_control.launch.xml

docs.title: Vehicle & System
docs.text:
Vehicle actuation and system diagnostics, run as separate containers from one image.

  • Vehicle — actuation and state reporting; steering, throttle, brake, gear, and turn-signal conversion; vehicle dimensions, limits, and kinematic parameters. Launch: tier4_vehicle_launch/vehicle.launch.xml
  • System — health monitoring and heartbeat management; diagnostic aggregation; Minimum Risk Maneuver handling; CPU, memory, and process monitoring. Launch: tier4_system_component.launch.xml

docs.title: API
docs.text:
Packages the Autoware AD API used by fleet managers, HMIs, and scenario runners. It provides ROS 2 services and topics for:

  • vehicle position, velocity, engage status, and operation mode
  • autonomous, manual, stop, local, and remote mode transitions
  • route and goal setting
  • emergency stop and engage/disengage commands
  • scenario simulation auto-engage and route integration

Launch: tier4_autoware_api_component.launch.xml. It is the external entry point of every deployment.

docs.title: Simulator
docs.text:
Closed-loop vehicle and environment simulation without real sensors or vehicle hardware:

  • configurable kinematic and dynamic vehicle models
  • dummy perception, vehicle, door, and traffic-infrastructure interfaces
  • Scenario Simulator v2 adapter and localization simulation mode
  • simulated point cloud preprocessing, object tracking, shape estimation, and map-based prediction
  • occupancy and elevation map handling; vehicle command conversion

Launch: tier4_simulator_component.launch.xml, with the perception simulation (dummy objects, tracking, prediction and the occupancy grid map) in its own perception-simulation service from planning_simulator/perception_simulation.launch.xml. On amd64 it also carries the CARLA bridge and the CARLA Python client that the CARLA Simulation deployment runs in its carla-interface service.

docs.title: Visualizer
docs.text:
RViz in the browser through noVNC: RViz with Autoware plugins, Openbox, TigerVNC, and a noVNC server over plain HTTP. The VNC backend stays loopback-only, and so does noVNC by default; reach it remotely through an SSH tunnel. To serve HTTPS, mount your own certificate into the visualizer from a kit (the release mounts none) and name its files in NOVNC_CERT and NOVNC_KEY; it stays the same across starts, so a browser exception for it holds.

Set these in the host settings file:

Variable Default Values Description RVIZ_CONFIG /tmp/openadkit/autoware_launch/share/autoware_launch/rviz/autoware.rviz Path RViz configuration inside the container; the default is the copy with config overrides applied REMOTE_DISPLAY true true, false RViz in the browser; false opens RViz on your own desktop instead, using the session's DISPLAY and XAUTHORITY REMOTE_PASSWORD openadkit String noVNC password, required when REMOTE_DISPLAY=true. The deployments set this default; the image itself has none WEBSOCKIFY_BIND 127.0.0.1 IP address noVNC bind address; bridge networking uses 0.0.0.0 with a host loopback port mapping USE_SIM_TIME false true, false Use the ROS simulation clock RVIZ_GPU auto auto, on, off Automatic, forced, or disabled VirtualGL acceleration NOVNC_CERT, NOVNC_KEY unset Paths Certificate and key inside the container; set both to serve HTTPS only

To open it, see the Quickstart.

docs.title: CARLA Interface
docs.text:
The simulator image's autoware_carla_interface translates Autoware control commands to CARLA and CARLA sensor data to ROS 2 messages:

  • CARLA world initialization and synchronous simulation
  • ego vehicle spawning and sensor-kit configuration
  • camera, LiDAR, IMU, and GNSS message translation
  • vehicle command calibration and traffic light state publication
  • lightweight sensor mappings for constrained hosts

Launch: autoware_carla_interface.launch.xml. CARLA publishes its Python client for x86_64 only, so only the amd64 simulator image has it (Humble and Jazzy); CARLA Simulation is Humble-only and needs an NVIDIA GPU.

docs.title: Deployments
docs.text:
A deployment is a ready-to-run Autoware stack for one task. New users should start with Planning Simulation.

Deployment Purpose GPU Architectures CI evidence Planning Simulation Plan and follow a route on a sample map with the built-in simulator; --gpu plans with the Diffusion Planner Optional amd64, arm64 Yes, in CPU mode Scenario Simulation Run predefined traffic scenarios in Scenario Simulator No amd64, arm64 Yes Logging Simulation Replay recorded sensor data through sensing, perception and localization Optional amd64, arm64 Exempt CARLA Simulation Drive in closed loop with the CARLA simulator Required amd64 Exempt Safety Island Simulation Planning Simulation driven by the Autoware Safety Island controller No amd64 Yes

All run on Humble and Jazzy except CARLA Simulation, which is Humble-only, and the GPU modes are amd64-only. CI evidence says whether a release runs the deployment end to end before it ships; an exempt deployment ships without that check, and evidence runs on amd64 only. See the Evidence Policy.

Scenario and CARLA Simulation can also run as split-host nodes, with Autoware on one host and the simulator on another over Zenoh (experimental).

docs.title: Running a Deployment
docs.text:
Complete the Quickstart setup first.

openadkit list
openadkit run planning-simulation
openadkit status
openadkit logs --follow
openadkit stop
  • Add --ros-distro jazzy to validate, fetch, run or build to select Jazzy; Humble is the default.
  • Add --gpu for the optional GPU mode of Planning Simulation (the Diffusion Planner) or Logging Simulation (CenterPoint). CARLA needs a GPU, so its GPU mode turns on by itself.
  • Put host settings in ~/.config/openadkit/<name>.env; see Configuration.

CLI & Maintenance covers the other commands.

docs.title: Your Own Kit
docs.text: Start a kit with openadkit new (Create a Kit). It extends a deployment without copying it and keeps only your differences. The Integrator Guide is the reference for every extension point.

docs.title: Split-host Simulation
docs.text:
Experimental

Split-host nodes may change in a minor release. See Compatibility.

Run the Autoware stack on one lab machine and the simulator on another, bridged over Zenoh. A deployment keeps its name and declares its nodes in deployment.json; each machine starts one node with --node:

  • scenario-simulation: --node autoware on one host, --node scenario on the other.
  • carla-simulation: --node autoware on one GPU host, --node carla on the other.

Without --node, the deployment runs on one host as usual.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
Each node has its own Compose entrypoint, compose.<node>.yaml, named in the manifest. It includes the node's services and ../shared/compose.zenoh.yaml, and mounts the deployment's config/zenoh.json5 allowlist. The CLI only selects the node's files and passes its rosDomainId as OPENADKIT_ROS_DOMAIN_ID; it adds no service of its own. The allowlist is one of the node's requiredFiles, so a missing or symlinked file fails validation before any container starts.

Each node is isolated: its own Compose project (openadkit-<deployment>_<node>), container names and ROS domain. The nodes see each other only through the Zenoh bridge, so both can also run on one machine for testing, as long as each listens on its own port (see below).

DDS stays on loopback (CYCLONEDDS_NETWORK_INTERFACE=lo) in the node's containers and in the bridge; a node ignores another interface in the host settings file. Only the ROS traffic on the deployment's allowlist crosses Zenoh: simulation time, vehicle status and commands, transforms, AD API calls, the enabled sensors and what the visualizer shows. Map blobs and camera images are not routed.

Evidence scope

  • In CI: both node views of each deployment validate, and Scenario Simulation's split evidence cell runs its two nodes on one hosted runner. The sample scenario passes over Zenoh, and the scenario node's ROS domain sees only the bridged topics, no Autoware nodes. CARLA is exempt from CI evidence.
  • By hand, on a lab pair: sample scenarios pass, and a CARLA goal reaches ArrivedGoal over the bridge.
  • Open: bridge restart resilience, and recorded CARLA throughput and latency.

One-runner evidence is not a general two-host, WAN or vehicle claim; see the Evidence Policy.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
On both hosts:

  • Host setup as in the Quickstart.
  • The same Open AD Kit release and ROS distro.
  • Layer-2/3 connectivity between the hosts and 7447/tcp open only between them. An allowlist is not authentication; do not expose the port to a WAN.

Fetch data on the hosts that mount it:

openadkit fetch scenario-simulation   # both hosts (the runner bind-mounts MAP_PATH)
openadkit fetch carla-simulation      # Autoware host only

docs.title: Configure the Bridge Endpoints
docs.text:
Create or edit ~/.config/openadkit/<deployment>.env on each host. Use the host's LAN IP, not 0.0.0.0:

Host Variables Autoware (--node autoware) ZENOH_LISTEN=tcp/<autoware-host-ip>:7447 Simulator (--node scenario or --node carla) ZENOH_LISTEN=tcp/<sim-host-ip>:7447 and ZENOH_PEER=tcp/<autoware-host-ip>:7447

The Autoware node only listens and starts first. validate and run on the connecting node fail fast when ZENOH_PEER is unset; stop, status and logs never need either variable.

To run both nodes on one machine, pass the endpoints per command instead, with a separate port for each node:

ZENOH_LISTEN=tcp/127.0.0.1:7447 openadkit run scenario-simulation --node autoware
ZENOH_LISTEN=tcp/127.0.0.1:7448 ZENOH_PEER=tcp/127.0.0.1:7447 \
  openadkit run scenario-simulation --node scenario

docs.title: Scenario Simulation
docs.text:
Start Autoware first, then the scenario host:

openadkit run scenario-simulation --node autoware   # Autoware host
openadkit run scenario-simulation --node scenario   # scenario host

The runner waits up to SCENARIO_READY_TIMEOUT for Autoware over Zenoh before it launches the scenario. Results are written on the scenario host under ~/openadkit-output/scenario-simulation/results. The visualizer runs there too, so RViz takes no CPU or GPU from Autoware on the edge.

docs.title: CARLA
docs.text:
Both hosts need an NVIDIA GPU. Start Autoware first, then the CARLA host:

openadkit run carla-simulation --node autoware   # Autoware host
openadkit run carla-simulation --node carla      # CARLA host

CARLA RPC (127.0.0.1:2000) and map loading stay local to the CARLA host. The interface publishes simulation time, the enabled LiDAR, IMU and GNSS sensors, vehicle status and transforms; Autoware publishes control commands. Cameras are disabled in sensor_mapping.yaml; enabling them requires an allowlist and throughput update. The visualizer runs on the CARLA host, where the raw LiDAR already originates.

docs.title: Allowlist
docs.text:
Each deployment ships its Zenoh allowlist in deployments/<deployment>/config/zenoh.json5, mounted into the bridge of every node. Entries are full-name regular expressions, not globs. Both hosts use the same file, since either side can own an endpoint. Review the list before routing anything new.

  • The visualizer's topics are on both allowlists: planning and control output, objects, the vector map marker, /robot_description and the AD API (/api/.*) its panels use. Zenoh sends a topic across only when the other host subscribes to it, so without a visualizer these stay on the edge.
  • CARLA's processed point clouds cross at 2 Hz (pub_max_frequencies); the point cloud map is not bridged.
  • /sensing/imu/imu_data of the simple sensor simulator is on the scenario allowlist because autonomous emergency braking and autonomous-mode availability on the Autoware host depend on it. Without it the vehicle stays in PLANNING and the scenario times out.

The split evidence cell checks that every allowlisted topic exists in one of the two graphs, so an Autoware rename fails CI instead of silently stopping a topic. CI cannot run CARLA: check its allowlist against the live graph of a two-host run after an Autoware update.

docs.title: Latency and Timing
docs.text: Cross-host simulation is timing sensitive. With a large round-trip time the TF stream jitters and control nodes log transform or collision-detector warnings even when scenarios still pass. Keep both hosts on the same lab LAN; WAN and VPN links are best-effort and are not the supported setup.

docs.title: Lifecycle Notes
docs.text:
• status, logs, restart, shell, record and stop find the running node from its Compose project, so you normally omit --node. When several nodes of one deployment run on the same machine, status and stop act on all of them; pass --node to choose one for the other commands.
  • Running a node that is already up updates it in place. Starting the single-host deployment while a node is running, or a node while the single-host deployment is running, is refused: stop it first.
  • With --verbose, the printed Compose command shows the node's files, env files and project name.
  • The visualizer is loopback-only on the simulator host (WEBSOCKIFY_BIND); reach it from another desk through an SSH tunnel.
  • Do not restart a single bridge or interface container while the split is running: route churn can leave a bridged topic half-connected. Stop and start the node instead (see Troubleshooting).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
If RViz shows no Auto button and /api/operation_mode/change_to_autonomous answers "The target mode is not available", a bridged vehicle-status topic has stopped flowing:

  • Diagnosis on the Autoware host: a state monitor logs a bridge topic timeout (for example /vehicle/status/steering_status topic is timeout), and /system/command_mode/availability reports autonomous mode unavailable.
  • Cause: restarting a single bridge or interface container in a running split can leave Zenoh routes half-created (a route is removed and not recreated), so the topic no longer crosses.
  • Remedy: stop the deployment on both hosts and start the nodes again (openadkit stop, then openadkit run <deployment> --node ...). A clean restart restores the routes.

docs.title: CARLA Simulation
docs.text: Run the full modular Autoware stack against CARLA 0.9.16 in closed loop.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• amd64 host with Ubuntu 22.04 (CARLA 0.9.16 is not validated on 24.04)
  • NVIDIA GPU with 16 GB of VRAM, with the NVIDIA Container Toolkit and the OpenGL/Vulkan libraries that openadkit setup --gpu installs
  • ROS 2 Humble images; this deployment does not support Jazzy

Complete the Quickstart setup with GPU support:

openadkit setup --gpu --verify

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
openadkit run carla-simulation

run downloads and verifies the Town01 map, then starts CARLA and the Autoware stack. CARLA renders offscreen by default. run returns once CARLA accepts connections and the services stay up; this deployment declares no readiness check of Autoware itself and is exempt from CI evidence.

To run Autoware and CARLA on separate hosts, see Split-host Simulation.

config/sensor_mapping.yaml enables LiDAR, IMU, and GNSS. Camera entries are available but commented out.

docs.title: Open the Visualizer
docs.text:
Open http://localhost:6080/vnc.html and sign in with the default password openadkit. To use your own, set REMOTE_PASSWORD in ~/.config/openadkit/<deployment>.env.

The visualizer listens on loopback only. For a remote host, forward the port over SSH and open http://localhost:8080/vnc.html locally:

ssh -L 8080:localhost:6080 <user>@<host>

In RViz, set a goal with 2D Goal Pose and select Auto.

docs.title: Stop and Recover
docs.text:
openadkit stop

Run stop also after a failed start, to release the GPU. If autonomous mode is unavailable, inspect /system/command_mode/availability and /diagnostics_graph/status. For other issues, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Logging Simulation
docs.text:
Replay a sample rosbag through sensing, perception and localization. An NVIDIA GPU with at least 4 GB of VRAM is recommended; CPU mode works but is much slower.

Complete the Quickstart setup first. For GPU mode, run openadkit setup --gpu --verify.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
openadkit run logging-simulation         # CPU: clustering-based detection
openadkit run logging-simulation --gpu   # GPU: CenterPoint on CUDA (amd64 only)

Add --ros-distro jazzy to select Jazzy; Humble is the default.

run downloads the sample map and rosbag, and with --gpu also the CenterPoint models (to ~/autoware_data/lidar_centerpoint). The rosbag starts playing once sensing subscribes to its LiDAR topic.

run returns once the services have started and stay up. This deployment declares no readiness check of Autoware itself and is exempt from CI evidence, so watch openadkit status and the visualizer for localization to initialize.

The sample rosbag is Copyright 2020 TIER IV, Inc. It has no camera images, so traffic-light recognition is unavailable and detection is less complete than with a full recording.

docs.text:
Open http://localhost:6080/vnc.html and sign in with the default password openadkit. To use your own, set REMOTE_PASSWORD in ~/.config/openadkit/<deployment>.env.

The visualizer listens on loopback only. For a remote host, forward the port over SSH and open http://localhost:8080/vnc.html locally:

ssh -L 8080:localhost:6080 <user>@<host>

docs.title: Stop and Recover

openadkit stop

To replace missing sample data, run openadkit fetch logging-simulation --force; it also refreshes the CenterPoint models. For other issues, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Planning Simulation
docs.text:
Run the Autoware planning and control stack on a sample map with the built-in simulator, then set a route in RViz in your browser. No GPU is required; with an NVIDIA GPU, --gpu plans with Autoware 2.0's Diffusion Planner.

Complete the Quickstart setup first. For GPU mode, run openadkit setup --gpu --verify.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
openadkit run planning-simulation         # CPU: the rule-based planner
openadkit run planning-simulation --gpu   # GPU: the Diffusion Planner (amd64 only)

Add --ros-distro jazzy to select Jazzy; Humble is the default.

run downloads the sample map, pulls the images and starts the stack. The sample map is Copyright 2020 TIER IV, Inc. and is provided for demonstration only.

docs.title: GPU Mode
docs.text:
Experimental

The GPU mode may change in a minor release. See Compatibility.

With --gpu, the planning service runs the planning-cuda image with planning_setting:=diffusion_planner, and run also downloads the Diffusion Planner v5.0 model from Hugging Face to ~/autoware_data/ml_models/diffusion_planner/v5.0. The first start builds a TensorRT engine from the model there, so it takes longer than later starts. The planner used about 0.8 GB of GPU memory in a measured run, engine build included; RViz renders on the CPU.

Control and the rest of the stack are the same in both modes: control follows /planning/trajectory, whichever planner makes it. See Autoware Architecture 2.0 for the planner. CI evidence runs the CPU mode; the GPU mode is checked by hand on a GPU host.

Known limitation

Autoware 2.0.0's Diffusion Planner can stop the ego up to about 2 m before the goal, so the route does not become ARRIVED and run --gpu --verify fails on the sample route. This is the planner's own output, reproduced with upstream's image (autoware_universe#13603).

docs.title: Safety Island Simulation
docs.text: Planning Simulation driven by the Autoware Safety Island instead of Autoware's own trajectory follower. Autoware runs on DDS domain 1, the Safety Island on domain 2, and domain_bridge connects them. No GPU is required.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• amd64 host: the pinned Safety Island release ships a linux/amd64 binary.
  • No GPU mode: the deployment's diagnostics graph belongs to the rule-based planner. validate and run refuse arm64 and --gpu.

Complete the Quickstart setup first.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
openadkit run safety-island-simulation

Add --ros-distro jazzy to select Jazzy; Humble is the default.

run downloads the sample map and the pinned Safety Island release, then starts Planning Simulation with two more services:

Service What it runs safety-island The release's actuation binary (FreeRTOS on POSIX) safety-island-bridge domain_bridge between the two domains, with the release's bridge-config.yaml topic contract

Autoware's trajectory follower is switched off, so the control command comes from the Safety Island alone. run returns once the bridge's healthcheck confirms it: the command's only publisher is the bridge, and the follower is not running.

Two messages are expected:

  • run warns that a config override adds autoware-safety-island.yaml, which autoware_launch does not have. The file is new: Autoware's main diagnostics graph without the follower's diagnostics.
  • The safety-island container logs Waiting for ... data until localization is initialized.

docs.title: Scenario Simulation
docs.text:
Run predefined traffic scenarios with TIER IV Scenario Simulator. The deployment runs a scenario automatically and writes the results to the host. No GPU is required.

Complete the Quickstart setup first.

openadkit run scenario-simulation
openadkit logs --follow

To run Autoware on one host and the scenario runner on another, see Split-host Simulation.

Add --ros-distro jazzy to select Jazzy; Humble is the default.

run downloads the Kashiwanoha map. Autoware takes about 90 seconds to initialize; the runner then executes the scenario and writes the results to ~/openadkit-output/scenario-simulation/results (run prints the path).

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
Set these in the host settings file, ~/.config/openadkit/scenario-simulation.env:

Variable Purpose Default SCENARIO Scenario path inside the container Bundled example SCENARIO_HOST_DIR Host scenario directory, mounted at /scenarios ./scenarios OUTPUT_HOST_PATH Host results directory ~/openadkit-output/scenario-simulation/results SCENARIO_READY_TIMEOUT Seconds to wait for Autoware before running 600 GLOBAL_REAL_TIME_FACTOR Simulated seconds per wall-clock second; below 1 on a host that cannot run Autoware in real time 1.0 GLOBAL_TIMEOUT Wall-clock seconds each scenario may take; scale it with the factor 180 MAP_PATH Host map directory ~/autoware_map/kashiwanoha_map

A relative SCENARIO_HOST_DIR resolves from deployments/scenario-simulation/. MAP_PATH must be absolute; use $HOME rather than ~.

To run your own scenario, keep it outside the release. Create a directory, put the YAML there, and point the deployment at it in the host settings file:

SCENARIO_HOST_DIR=$HOME/openadkit-scenarios
SCENARIO=/scenarios/my-scenario.yaml

The default ./scenarios lies inside the installed release: files placed there mark the deployment as modified and are lost on upgrade or uninstall.

Scenarios must match the map, and the planning sample map does not work here. To use your own map, point MAP_PATH at a directory that holds the same files as the bundled map, which the CLI checks before starting: lanelet2_map.osm, pointcloud_map.pcd, global_map_center.pcd.yaml, lanelet2_map_provider.osm.yaml and map.map_publisher.yaml.

This deployment changes one Autoware parameter with a config override: a file that holds only the changed value, merged into the upstream parameter file on every start (config/autoware/autoware_default_adapi_universe/config/default_adapi.param.yaml).

docs.title: Build from Source
docs.text: How to build the Open AD Kit images locally and how CI builds them. Most users do not need this: openadkit run pulls the published images (see Container Images & Versioning).

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04 (openadkit setup supports Ubuntu only; elsewhere, install Docker with Buildx and Compose yourself)
  • Git; step 3 installs the tools that import the Autoware sources
  • Disk space for several multi-gigabyte images

The component Dockerfiles build on upstream Autoware images from GHCR and compile their package sets from a local autoware/src tree (step 4 below).

docs.title: Build System
docs.text:
Images are built with Docker Bake from components/docker-bake.hcl, the same file CI uses.

flowchart TB
    CORE["autoware:core-devel (build)<br/>autoware:base (runtime)"] --> UC["universe-common"]
    CORE --> UCD["universe-common-devel<br/>(kits build their overlays in it)"]
    CUDA["autoware:base-cuda-{devel,runtime}"] --> SPC["sensing-perception-cuda"]
    CUDA --> PLC["planning-cuda"]

    UC --> SP["sensing-perception"]
    UC --> LM["localization-mapping"]
    UC --> PLN["planning"]
    UC --> CTL["control"]
    UC --> VS["vehicle-system"]
    UC --> API["api"]
    UC --> VIZ["visualizer"]
    UC --> SIM["simulator"]
    UC -.-> SPC
    UC -.-> PLC

universe-common compiles the shared part of Autoware Universe on the upstream core-devel image and copies the result onto the lean upstream base image, so build tools never reach the runtime layers. Every component builds from it. The CUDA variants, sensing-perception-cuda and planning-cuda, build on the upstream CUDA images and add the universe-common install tree.

The published images end with a per-build Ubuntu security refresh. Components compile on universe-common-build, the devel image without that refresh, which CI pushes only to its build cache. Its digest changes only with its inputs, so a build that changes no Autoware source or component Dockerfile reuses the cached compiles and only refreshes and reassembles the runtime images.

Group Targets universe-common universe-common-devel, universe-common component all component images, including the amd64-only sensing-perception-cuda and planning-cuda planning-simulation universe-common plus the images Planning Simulation needs (local builds) default universe-common + component

CI publishes every image to ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/openadkit.

docs.title: Build and Run Locally
docs.text:
# 1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/autowarefoundation/openadkit.git
cd openadkit

# 2. Install host dependencies
./openadkit setup --verify

Activate the Docker group membership added by openadkit setup before running Docker without sudo. Either log out and back in, or run:

newgrp docker

# 3. Install the source import tools; pipx puts vcs in ~/.local/bin
sudo apt-get install -y pipx python3-yaml
pipx install vcs2l
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

# 4. Import the Autoware sources this branch pins
AUTOWARE_REF=$(cat .github/autoware.ref)
git init autoware
git -C autoware fetch --depth 1 \
  https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.git "$AUTOWARE_REF"
git -C autoware checkout --detach FETCH_HEAD
# An Autoware release, built on its official images
python3 .github/scripts/export_autoware_lock.py \
  autoware/repositories/autoware.repos autoware.lock
export UPSTREAM_TAG="$AUTOWARE_REF"
mkdir -p autoware/src
vcs import --shallow autoware/src < autoware.lock
# Backported Autoware fixes, when the branch carries any
python3 .github/scripts/autoware_patches.py apply autoware/src
mkdir -p autoware/src/middleware/external
touch autoware/src/middleware/external/.keep

# 5. Build the shared universe-common layer (~2 hours)
docker buildx bake -f components/docker-bake.hcl universe-common

# 6. Build the Planning Simulation images (~2 hours)
docker buildx bake -f components/docker-bake.hcl --load planning-simulation

# 7. Run with the local images
./openadkit run planning-simulation
  • --load puts the images in the local Docker store; without it, Bake only fills the build cache.
  • Local builds are tagged <target>-<arch>-<ros-distro> (for example planning-amd64-humble), which is the tag ./openadkit looks up in a source checkout. The arch follows the build host; when cross-building, set tags with --set <target>.tags=.... To use other images, set the *_IMAGE variables in ~/.config/openadkit/<deployment>.env.
  • For Jazzy, build with ROS_DISTRO=jazzy and run with --ros-distro jazzy.

Other useful targets:

docker buildx bake -f components/docker-bake.hcl                                # everything
docker buildx bake -f components/docker-bake.hcl component                      # all components
docker buildx bake -f components/docker-bake.hcl --load sensing-perception      # one image

docs.title: Build Variables
docs.text: Variable Description Default ROS_DISTRO humble or jazzy humble UPSTREAM_TAG Upstream Autoware release to build on, the tag in .github/autoware.ref (e.g. 2.0.0); required "" UPSTREAM_REPO Upstream Autoware image repository ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware ROS_SNAPSHOT_HUMBLE, ROS_SNAPSHOT_JAZZY ROS apt snapshot the UPSTREAM_TAG images were built from. The build fails when they do not match; see ROS snapshot. Snapshots for 2.0.0

docs.title: Continuous Integration
docs.text:
build-all-images.yaml builds every target with the same Bake file. The build matrix comes from .github/image-inventory.json, the source of truth for which images are built and for which architectures.

Jobs run in dependency order: prepare, then build-common, then build-components. Most images build for Humble and Jazzy on amd64 and arm64. create-manifests then combines the per-arch images into multi-arch tags. CI disables the local tags (LOCAL_IMAGE="") and tags images through docker/metadata-action.

.github/autoware.ref pins the Autoware release a branch builds on its official images. CI builds main and release/* pushes, keeps registry caches per branch, and scans and runs the evidence cells after each build. A weekly scan of main's latest build opens a GitHub issue when it fails.

A pull request builds only the images its changes affect; see Testing a Pull Request. Releases promote one of these builds; see the Release Process.

docs.title: Evidence Workflow
docs.text: .github/workflows/evidence.yaml runs the evidence cells against one build and publishes the run's summary. It runs after every successful build-all-images run on main or a release/X.Y branch, which is the run a release of that build needs.

docs.title: Testing a Pull Request
docs.text:
A pull request that changes an image's inputs builds the affected images, amd64 only, for both distros. A pull request from this repository pushes them to the CI package openadkit-ci, completes the build there with its base branch's other images, copied by digest, and runs the cells on that build before merge. A fork's pull request cannot push; its images are checked at the build and scan only, and run in the cells after merge.

A change that rebuilds no image, such as a deployment setting, the CLI or a check, runs the cells against an existing build:

  • A pull request that touches deployments/, cli/ or the evidence checks runs them against its base branch's latest successful build.
  • A dispatch of evidence.yaml with source_ref tests that branch or commit; build_tag defaults to the dispatched branch's latest successful build.

The cells take the deployments, CLI and checks from the tested commit and the images from the build. A pull request's run is not release evidence: the gate accepts only a run on the release branch that tested the build's own commit.

docs.title: Reuse It for an Existing Build
docs.text:
A caller workflow in the same repository (or in a fork that hosts the same build and evidence workflows) can call it without duplicating the runner:

name: verify-existing-build
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      build_tag:
        description: Build run ID and attempt, e.g. 123456789-1
        required: true
        type: string

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: read

jobs:
  evidence:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/evidence.yaml
    with:
      build_tag: ${{ inputs.build_tag }}

This runs containers on the caller's runners. A fork's evidence runs belong to that fork; only runs on the branch that built the release, in the releasing repository, can be release evidence.

The reusable interface takes only build_tag. It does not take an external kit repository, revision or scenario as input, so do not copy this example into an unrelated repository and claim it verifies that kit: external kits need a dedicated, pinned, trusted-builder implementation first.

docs.title: Inputs, Outputs and Boundaries
docs.text:
• Input: build_tag has the form <run_id>-<run_attempt>. The matching build-metadata-<build_tag> artifact must be available in the repository.
  • What it tests: the workflow checks out the build's openadkit_sha and takes the image digests from the same metadata, never latest aliases. It stages the kit with the same step that assembles release bundles, so the cells run the tree a release of that build ships, plus the example kit. The staged CLI's openadkit new makes that kit, with the fixture in .github/scripts/evidence/kit on top; its workspace builds against the build's universe-common-devel digest for each distro.
  • How it runs: hosted runners execute the L0-L3 cells, retry a failed cell once, and aggregate every expected cell; a missing cell fails the run.
  • Output: per-cell diagnostics and the evidence-summary-<build_tag> artifact, which the release gate reads.

Cells use schemaVersion: 1, and the summary (schemaVersion: 3) carries them as written. Readers accept only these versioned payloads: a cell without schemaVersion: 1 and metrics is rejected. Read timings from metrics rather than from top-level fields. Source and config checksums leave out the build, install and log products of a workspace.

docs.title: Release Process
docs.text: For maintainers. A release promotes an existing CI build of its branch; nothing is rebuilt. The Evidence Policy says what a build must pass, and Compatibility what a version number promises.

docs.title: Before You Release
docs.text:
• The branch: main, or a release/X.Y branch created from a release tag to fix an older line. Its .github/autoware.ref names the Autoware release (for example 2.0.0), and the ROS snapshots in components/docker-bake.hcl belong to that release.
  • vars.RUNNER_AMD64 and vars.RUNNER_ARM64 optionally move the build, scan and evidence jobs to larger runners (for example ubicloud-standard-8-ubuntu-2204 and ubicloud-standard-8-arm-ubuntu-2204). Unset, they run on the GitHub-hosted ubuntu-22.04 and ubuntu-22.04-arm. Pull request jobs run on them too, so point them only at ephemeral hosted runners, never at a persistent self-hosted machine.
  • GHCR packages accept pushes from CI: openadkit, openadkit-buildcache and openadkit-ci under ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/.
  • secrets.RELEASE_TOKEN (Contents and Workflows write) is set when promoting a build commit older than later workflow changes; otherwise GITHUB_TOKEN is used.
  • A successful build of build-all-images exists on that branch; stable releases and pre-releases both come from it. The build summary shows its build_tag. The release ships the CLI and deployments of that build's commit. A push that changes only the CLI or deployments starts no build, so dispatch build-all-images on the branch to release it; the release run warns when the branch has such changes.
  • A passing scan of scan-images exists for that build_tag on the same branch; it runs after the build.
  • A successful evidence run on the same branch passed every cell for that same build; it runs after the build. See the Evidence Policy.
  • Highlights for a minor or major release are in .github/release-highlights/vX.Y.Z.md. The notes of that release and of its candidates open with them; the rest of the notes is generated.
  • The roadmap is reviewed for a minor or major release: finished items are gone, the release's items are under Now, and its Last reviewed line names the release. Validation checks that line for the release and its candidates.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
Run release.yaml on the build's branch with the version and build_tag. A release/X.Y branch releases with its own workflows and scripts, so a later main cannot change how an older line is validated. Its jobs run in order:

flowchart LR
    V[validate] --> P[package-bundles] --> R[publish] --> O[deploy-docs]
  1. validate: runs the release gates in validate_release.sh (version format, roadmap review, build provenance and age, scan results, metadata and file integrity, image coverage, passing evidence, registry digests, Git tag). A build older than 90 days cannot be promoted. Nothing is tagged if a gate fails.
  2. package-bundles: writes the immutable release plan and the runtime bundle for both distros.
  3. publish: writes the notes and metadata from the validated plan, attests the bundle, installer, plan and metadata, and creates the draft with its assets. It then creates the image release tags and, for stable releases, the latest aliases (see Tag Reference), and publishes the draft, which creates the Git tag. A published release cannot be changed: a bad one is followed by the next version.
  4. deploy-docs: republishes the docs when the latest aliases moved.

The release plan (release-plan.json) attached to each GitHub Release records the exact image digests, aliases, assets, and checksums of that release.

A fork can rehearse a release with the same workflow: it promotes its own build in its own registry namespace and publishes in the fork. Validation only requires the registry and the package name that openadkit.json names.

docs.title: Backporting an Autoware Fix
docs.text:
Autoware releases come months apart. A fix that blocks a release and is upstream, merged on Autoware's main or in an open pull request, can ride on the pinned release as a patch instead of waiting for the next Autoware release:

  1. In the upstream repository, git format-patch -1 <commit>, and add a line Upstream: <URL of the commit or pull request> to its message.
  2. Open a pull request into main (or the release/X.Y branch) that adds it as .github/autoware-patches/<repository>/<NNNN>-<subject>.patch, where <repository> is its path under autoware/src (a key of autoware-lock.repos, such as universe/autoware_universe). The review is the fix's own diff.
  3. Every build applies the patches in order right after vcs import; one that does not apply, or has no Upstream: line, fails the build. The release lists them under Backported Autoware fixes, its bundle carries them as autoware.backports, and openadkit version counts them. The Autoware version stays that of the tag.
  4. When the branch moves to an Autoware release that contains the fix, delete the patch.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
From zero to a running Autoware planning simulation in about 10 minutes. No GPU is required.

  1. 1 InstallOne command
  2. 2 Set up the hostConfigure dependencies
  3. 3 Run simulationStart planning
  4. 4 Open visualizerInspect the output
  5. 5 DriveSet a route

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ubuntu 22.04 (Jammy) or 24.04 (Noble) with sudo access
  • 8 CPU cores, 16 GB of RAM and 50 GB of storage or more; see Hardware
  • curl for the release installer; python3 and tar are preinstalled on supported Ubuntu releases
  • A web browser: the visualizer runs in it, so no display server is needed

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
v2.0.0 is not published yet

Until the first stable release there is no release bundle to install. A source checkout runs images you build yourself; see Build from Source.

curl -fsSL https://github.com/autowarefoundation/openadkit/releases/latest/download/openadkit \
  | bash -s -- install

The installer verifies the release bundle, installs it to ~/.local/share/openadkit and puts openadkit in ~/.local/bin. If that directory is not on your PATH, it prints the command to add it. The bundle holds the CLI and the deployments; images and sample data are pulled on demand.

Pin a version, or check the files first

For a reproducible install, replace latest with a release version and pass the same version to install:

curl -fsSL https://github.com/autowarefoundation/openadkit/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/openadkit \
  | bash -s -- install --version vX.Y.Z

To check the files yourself before running them, see Verify a Release.

docs.title: 2. Set Up the Host
docs.text:
openadkit setup --verify

Run setup as your normal user; it asks for sudo only for host changes. It installs Docker when the host has none and never replaces an existing engine. Add --gpu for NVIDIA deployments: it also installs the NVIDIA Container Toolkit and the OpenGL/Vulkan libraries CARLA needs.

Activate the Docker group membership added by openadkit setup before running Docker without sudo. Either log out and back in, or run:

newgrp docker

docs.title: 3. Run Planning Simulation
docs.text:
openadkit run planning-simulation

run downloads and verifies the sample map, pulls missing images, starts the services, and returns once Autoware is ready.

Add --ros-distro jazzy to select Jazzy; Humble is the default.

docs.title: 4. Open the Visualizer
docs.text:
Open http://localhost:6080/vnc.html and sign in with the default password openadkit. To use your own, set REMOTE_PASSWORD in ~/.config/openadkit/<deployment>.env.

The visualizer listens on loopback only. For a remote host, forward the port over SSH and open http://localhost:8080/vnc.html locally:

ssh -L 8080:localhost:6080 <user>@<host>

To open RViz on your own desktop instead of the browser, see Visualizer.

docs.title: 5. Drive
docs.text:
In RViz, follow the Autoware planning simulation instructions to:

  1. Set an initial pose for the ego vehicle
  2. Set a goal pose on the map
  3. Watch the vehicle plan and drive the route

docs.title: When You Are Done
docs.text:
openadkit stop

stop removes the containers. The images and the sample map stay on the host, so the next run starts faster.

docs.title: CLI & Maintenance
docs.text:
The commands you need after the first run. openadkit --help and openadkit <command> --help list every option.

Commands on this page are shown as installed by the release installer. From a source checkout, prefix them with ./ and run them from the repository root.

Command What it does list, run List the deployments, and start one and wait until it is ready status, logs, shell, record Inspect the running deployment and record its topics restart Apply changed settings, config and overlay workspaces stop Stop and remove the running deployment validate, config Check a deployment, or print its Compose model, without starting it fetch, clean Download or delete a deployment's data new, build Create a kit and build its overlay workspace setup Install the host dependencies install, upgrade, uninstall Install, move between and remove releases version Show the installed release and its Autoware release

docs.title: Run a Deployment
docs.text:
openadkit list                                    # the deployments you can run
openadkit run planning-simulation
openadkit run planning-simulation --verify        # then run its end-to-end check
openadkit run planning-simulation --pull always   # refresh the images first
openadkit run planning-simulation --no-visualizer

run downloads missing data, pulls missing images, starts the services and returns once the deployment is ready.

  • Ready means the services' healthchecks pass, for example once the AD API is up (READINESS_CHECKS in the deployment's settings.env). run then watches the services for 10 seconds and fails if one crashes, restarts, exits or turns unhealthy; a one-shot service may finish but not fail.
  • --verify then runs the deployment's verify step, the check CI runs on it: Planning Simulation drives the ego from its start to its goal, Scenario Simulation waits for the scenarios' result. run exits with the step's result; the deployment keeps running.
  • --no-visualizer starts everything except the visualizer, for a host nobody watches: its software-rendered RViz needs CPU that Autoware lacks on a small host. CI evidence runs this way.
  • One deployment runs at a time, including deployments from other kits, even one with the same name. run refuses while another is running; stop it first with openadkit stop. The nodes of one split-host deployment can run together.

Every run writes results/run.json in the deployment's output directory: the version, distro and images it started, the digest of the resolved Compose model, content digests of the config layers and overlay workspace it mounts, how long it took to be ready and, with --verify, the step's result.

docs.title: Runtime Controls
docs.text:
openadkit status
openadkit logs --follow
openadkit logs map planning        # only these services
openadkit restart                  # apply changed settings, config and overlay workspaces
openadkit restart --all            # recreate the whole deployment
openadkit shell                    # a shell in the api service with ROS sourced
openadkit shell planning ros2 node list
openadkit record /tf /localization/kinematic_state
openadkit stop

These act on the deployment running on this host, from any directory, so they take no deployment name. With several nodes of a split-host deployment on one host, see Lifecycle Notes.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
Below its services, status shows Autoware's state from the AD API and the visualizer address:

localization initialized
routing      set
mode         stop (autonomous available)
mrm          normal

A line reads no data while nothing publishes that state yet, for example before localization starts.

docs.title: Restart
docs.text:
restart recreates services as run started them, with the current settings, config and overlay workspace, and keeps to the same readiness checks.

  • With no service, it recreates every service that takes Open AD Kit config or an overlay workspace, and every service whose settings changed. A changed parameter file, a rebuilt workspace or a new settings.env value applies without restarting a simulator such as CARLA; restart names the services it left running.
  • restart <service>... recreates only those services.
  • restart --all recreates the whole deployment, one-shot services included.

docs.title: Shell
docs.text: shell sources ROS, Autoware and the overlay workspace like the services' entrypoint. Give it a service and a command to run one command instead of an interactive shell.

docs.title: Record
docs.text: record writes a rosbag of the named topics (or --all) to ~/openadkit-output/<deployment>/recordings/ (--output to change) until Ctrl+C. It runs as a copy of the running api container, so it joins the deployment's ROS domain and knows the overlay's message types, and the bag stays on the host when the deployment stops.

docs.title: Validate Before Running
docs.text:
openadkit validate planning-simulation --data

validate checks the manifest and the Compose configuration without starting anything. --data also reports each data resource as ok, missing, incomplete or outdated and fails on any gap. It follows the same GPU selection as run: openadkit validate logging-simulation --gpu --data includes the CenterPoint models.

config prints a deployment's resolved Compose model as JSON, with validate's --ros-distro, --gpu, --node and --ws; AutoSD builds on it.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
A deployment reads its settings from environment files, in this order (later files win):

  1. deployments/<name>/settings.env: the deployment defaults
  2. deployments/<name>/settings.gpu.env: GPU settings, loaded only with --gpu
  3. ~/.config/openadkit/<name>.env: your host settings file

Shell exports do not override variables defined in these files. Put host settings such as MAP_PATH or REMOTE_PASSWORD in your host settings file: it lives outside the release, so upgrades keep it. A source checkout can also override component images there; release images stay pinned. A kit adds its own files to this order; see the Integrator Guide.

Directory Default Override Host settings ~/.config/openadkit OPENADKIT_CONFIG_DIR (or XDG_CONFIG_HOME) Results and recordings ~/openadkit-output/<name>/{results,recordings} OPENADKIT_OUTPUT_DIR Installed releases ~/.local/share/openadkit OPENADKIT_INSTALL_DIR

docs.title: Downloaded Data
docs.text:
Maps, rosbags and models live under ~/autoware_map and ~/autoware_data.

openadkit validate planning-simulation --data   # report
openadkit fetch planning-simulation --force     # replace
openadkit clean planning-simulation             # delete, after asking
  • run downloads missing data but never replaces an existing data directory; run --force is not supported.
  • fetch --force replaces incomplete or outdated data. Data is outdated when the deployment now declares other content for it, for example a map with a new checksum: run, fetch and validate --data then stop and ask for fetch --force. fetch always includes the GPU data.
  • clean lists what it deletes and asks first; --yes skips the question, as scripts need. It deletes all the data the deployment uses, so a kit or a deployment on a base also deletes the base's data (the list says so). The next run or fetch downloads it again.

The CLI marks the data it installs with a .openadkit-resource.json file, and clean and --force only delete or replace marked data. Data that was already there, such as a map you copied yourself, is used when it is complete, but the CLI never deletes or replaces it; move or remove it yourself.

clean and fetch --force refuse while that deployment is running, or while any live container mounts the data (including another kit or deployment). If data usage cannot be checked, they refuse as well.

docs.title: Your Own Kit
docs.text: openadkit new my-kit [--base DEPLOYMENT] makes ./my-kit, a kit on top of a deployment of this Open AD Kit (Planning Simulation by default) that holds only your differences. openadkit build builds the kit's overlay workspace in the release's devel image. See Create a Kit.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
openadkit upgrade --check   # report whether a newer stable version exists
openadkit upgrade           # install it

The new release is verified and installed next to the old one, and the openadkit launcher is repointed. The previous version stays in the install directory, so you can roll back:

openadkit install --version vOLD

A version that is already installed becomes the active one as it is, without a download, so this works offline; --force downloads and replaces it. Images of a version you no longer use stay in Docker until you remove them, for example with docker image prune --all. A source checkout updates with git pull instead.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
Stop running deployments first; uninstall refuses while any is running, because it removes the launcher that openadkit stop needs.

openadkit stop
openadkit uninstall          # keep previously installed versions
openadkit uninstall --all    # remove kept versions too

uninstall is for release installs; remove a source checkout with Git. It keeps your host settings in ~/.config/openadkit, results and recordings in ~/openadkit-output, and downloaded data.

docs.title: Names, Directories and Output
docs.text:
• A directory instead of a name: validate, config, fetch, run and clean also take a deployment's directory, such as openadkit run ./my-kit. An argument with a / or a leading . is a directory, and the kit around it is used wherever you run the command.
  • Version: openadkit version prints the installed release and the Autoware release it pins; in a source checkout, the commit.
  • Scripting: list, version and validate accept --json. validate --json prints one JSON document also when the deployment is invalid ("valid": false with the "error").
  • Docker commands: commands print what they do in plain terms; add --verbose (or set OPENADKIT_VERBOSE=1) to also see the docker commands they run, status queries aside.
  • Short name and Tab completion: openadkit install also links adkit, a short name for the same launcher. Tab completes commands, options and deployment names for both names, from the kit around the current directory or else the active release; bash-completion (installed on Ubuntu by default) loads it from ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions in a new shell. The installer leaves an adkit or a completion file it did not install alone, and openadkit uninstall removes only its own links.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Commands on this page are shown as installed by the release installer. From a source checkout, prefix them with ./ and run them from the repository root.

docs.title: A Deployment Fails to Start
docs.text:
1. Check that Docker is running: docker info.
  2. Check the configuration and the data: openadkit validate <deployment> --data.
  3. See which services are up: openadkit status.
  4. Read the logs: openadkit logs --follow.

If run fails after the containers are created, they keep running so you can read their logs. Stop them with openadkit stop.

docs.title: Permission denied
docs.text: Your user must be in the docker group. Log out and back in after openadkit setup, or run newgrp docker. Do not run openadkit with sudo.

docs.title: Docker Compose is too old
docs.text: openadkit setup stops when Docker is installed but Docker Compose 5.0 or newer is missing. Install Docker's docker-compose-plugin (instructions) and rerun setup. Ubuntu's own docker-compose-v2 package is too old.

docs.title: Missing or incomplete maps, rosbags, or models
docs.text:
openadkit validate <deployment> --data
openadkit fetch <deployment> --force

validate --data reports each resource as ok, missing, incomplete or outdated; add --gpu to include the data of a GPU mode, such as Logging Simulation's CenterPoint models. fetch always includes it. --force only replaces data the CLI installed; remove data you placed yourself, then run openadkit fetch <deployment>. See Downloaded Data.

docs.title: NVIDIA Container Toolkit not detected
docs.text:
• Install it with openadkit setup --gpu --verify.
  • Check the GPU: nvidia-smi and nvidia-ctk --version.
  • Restart Docker: sudo systemctl restart docker.

docs.title: Perception is slow
docs.text: The default perception image runs on CPU. For CUDA perception, run Logging Simulation with --gpu on an amd64 host with an NVIDIA GPU. The CUDA image does not fall back to CPU.

docs.title: Blank visualizer
docs.text: Wait 10 to 30 seconds after run, then reload the page. If it stays blank, check openadkit logs --follow.

docs.title: noVNC says "failed to connect"
docs.text: Open the page over http://. The visualizer serves plain HTTP unless you give it a certificate (NOVNC_CERT, NOVNC_KEY); with one, open it over https://.

docs.title: Port 6080 already in use
docs.text: Port 6080 serves the visualizer. Stop the service that holds the port. The deployments use host networking, so a ports: mapping in docker-compose.yaml has no effect.

docs.title: Point clouds arrive at a lower rate than they are published
docs.text:
Large messages need large UDP buffers between the containers. deployments/shared/cyclonedds.xml requests them, and openadkit setup raises the kernel limits that cap them (/etc/sysctl.d/99-openadkit-dds.conf). Check the limit and whether the kernel drops packets:

sysctl net.core.rmem_max      # 2147483647 after setup
nstat -az UdpRcvbufErrors     # a growing count means drops

docs.title: ROS 2 nodes on another machine cannot see the stack
docs.text:
DDS stays on loopback by default. To reach other hosts, set CYCLONEDDS_NETWORK_INTERFACE to the exact LAN or VPN interface name in your host settings file (~/.config/openadkit/<deployment>.env):

CYCLONEDDS_NETWORK_INTERFACE=eth0

This applies to single-host runs; a split-host node always keeps DDS on loopback and reaches the other host through its Zenoh bridge. ROS_DOMAIN_ID separates traffic but provides no authentication or encryption.
