docs.title: Create a Kit
docs.text:
openadkit new makes a kit that extends this Open AD Kit and one of its deployments without copying them, so the kit holds only your differences:

openadkit new my-kit                       # on top of planning-simulation
openadkit new my-kit --base scenario-simulation

docs.title: One Directory, One Deployment
docs.text:
my-kit/
├── openadkit.json
├── deployment.json
├── docker-compose.yaml
├── settings.env
├── config/autoware/
└── overlay_ws/src/
  • openadkit.json selects the base (extends), lists extra images you pin (externalImages), and points the my-kit deployment at ".", this same directory.
  • deployment.json names the base deployment. Compose reads docker-compose.yaml unless compose.files names others. Architecture, ROS distro, GPU, downloads and the verify step are inherited; requirements may narrow the first three.
  • docker-compose.yaml includes ${OPENADKIT_BASE_DEPLOYMENT}/docker-compose.yaml; add your services below it. OPENADKIT_BASE_ROOT names the base root for shared assets.
  • settings.env holds only the values you change, such as VEHICLE_ID.
  • config/autoware/ holds parameter overrides for Autoware packages.
  • overlay_ws/src/ holds your ROS packages.

The deployment's name is its key in openadkit.json, here my-kit; deployment.json does not repeat it. Renaming the directory changes nothing.

docs.title: Pin Your Base
docs.text: openadkit new from an installed release writes its version, such as "extends": "v2.0.0"; the kit then runs with that release's own launcher. From a source checkout it writes the checkout's path. To move to another release, change extends; the next command that acts on the kit, such as validate or run, downloads that release if it is missing.

docs.title: Build, Validate, Run, Stop
docs.text:
cd my-kit
openadkit build                 # overlay_ws, in the release's devel image
openadkit validate
openadkit run --verify          # start, wait until ready, run the base's end-to-end check
openadkit stop

Inside a kit with one deployment the commands need no name. From elsewhere, name it by its directory: openadkit run ./my-kit. A kit on a source checkout needs DEVEL_IMAGE for build; see Overlay Workspace.

Add --ros-distro jazzy to build, validate and run for Jazzy. validate renders the Compose model without starting anything; it is not runtime or ABI evidence, so finish with run --verify.

Every release tests a kit made this way: the example kit exercises each extension point on Humble and Jazzy.

docs.title: Where Changes Go
docs.text: Keep parameter changes in config/autoware/ and packages in overlay_ws/ rather than mounting over /opt/autoware or replacing a base service's command. The Integrator Guide is the reference for the settings order, config overrides, the overlay workspace, extra services and image replacement.

docs.title: Integrator Guide
docs.text: The reference for a kit: what it pins, each extension point, and how it is validated and upgraded. A kit owns its differences; Open AD Kit owns the base CLI, images and deployments. Start one with openadkit new (Create a Kit).

docs.title: Pin the Base
docs.text:
In the kit's openadkit.json, kind is kit and extends names a published release tag or, for development, the path of a source checkout. Manifests use schemaVersion: 2; older ones are rejected.

  • The pinned release runs the kit. The CLI finds it under ~/.local/share/openadkit/openadkit-<tag> (OPENADKIT_INSTALL_DIR to change) and hands the command to its launcher. A missing version is downloaded and verified on first use, as a build tool's wrapper does; your active openadkit stays as it is.
  • Only the commands that act on a kit do this: validate, config, fetch, run, build and clean. list, version, new, every --help and Tab completion read the kit with the CLI you called, so a directory you only look at starts no program and no download.
  • One level of extends: a kit extends Open AD Kit, not another kit.

docs.title: Base a Deployment
docs.text:
Each kit deployment names a base deployment of the pinned release in its deployment.json.

  • Requirements (architectures, ROS distros, GPU) are inherited. requirements may narrow them: fewer architectures or ROS distros, or gpu set to none or required where the base leaves it optional. It never widens them, since the kit runs the base's services. Without a GPU mode, the base's GPU-only downloads are left out.
  • Downloads and one-shot reset services are inherited. A kit can add downloads with distinct destination variables, and reset services of its own.
  • Split-host nodes are not inherited: a kit deployment runs on one host.

A kit made by openadkit new my-kit has one deployment, also named my-kit. Its manifests, Compose file and differences live in one directory (deployments.my-kit.path is "."), so it needs no nested deployments/ directory. Run commands from that directory, where they need no deployment name.

docs.title: 1. Settings
docs.text:
Put only differences in your deployment's settings.env. Compose reads these files in order (later files win):

  1. Base settings.env
  2. Base settings.gpu.env, when GPU mode is selected
  3. Kit settings.env, if present
  4. Kit settings.gpu.env, if present and GPU mode is selected
  5. ~/.config/openadkit/<kit-deployment>.env, if present

Shell exports do not override values set in these files. The CLI adds the ROS distro, the host UID and GID, the overlay mount paths, OPENADKIT_BASE_ROOT (the base's root) and OPENADKIT_BASE_DEPLOYMENT (the directory of the base deployment); a release's component and external images stay pinned. Inside the containers, the ROS and DDS defaults come from the base services' runtime.env.

docs.title: 2. Config Overrides
docs.text:
Store overrides under config/autoware/<package>/<path-relative-to-package-share>. For example, config/autoware/autoware_control_config/config/lane_departure_checker/lane_departure_checker.param.yaml:

/**:
  ros__parameters:
    update_rate: 20.0

On each start, the entrypoint hook copies the package share directory into /tmp/openadkit/<package>/share/<package>. It applies the shared, base-deployment and kit-deployment layers in that order. YAML mappings merge recursively; scalars and lists replace the old value. Launch substitutions such as $(var ...) stay intact. Non-YAML files replace their counterpart.

The copied prefixes go first on AMENT_PREFIX_PATH, and base launch arguments use the same stable paths. No change is written into the image. Removing an override and restarting returns to the remaining layers.

Unknown packages, files or YAML keys are warnings, not startup failures. The hook logs them and writes /tmp/openadkit/overlay-report.json in each container. Once the services are up, run collects those reports and warns about every override without a counterpart: a package no service has changes nothing, and a file or a parameter its package does not have is added. That is intended for a new file such as a diagnostics graph; after a base version change it usually means a renamed package, file or parameter. Every service gets the same layers, so a package installed in only some images is not reported.

docs.title: A New Vehicle
docs.text:
Autoware's defaults describe a passenger car. Review these for your vehicle; their package and path depend on the base's Autoware version, so look them up in its images and check run's override warnings.

Parameters File Why Dimensions, wheel_base, max_steer_angle vehicle_info.param.yaml of your vehicle description Planning and control use them as limits; a steering limit above the vehicle's makes control ask for angles it cannot reach. Sensor poses your sensor kit's sensor_kit_calibration.yaml and sensors_calibration.yaml A wrong sign or offset shows up as a localization error of the same size. nominal_latency, assumed_limit_acc control_validator.param.yaml Your actuation latency and achievable braking. With car values a slower or weaker vehicle fails validation and triggers an MRM. pose_measurement.pose_gate_dist ekf_localizer.param.yaml The Mahalanobis gate for pose updates. A start pose far from the truth can be rejected for good. Velocity, acceleration, jerk and steering-rate limits vehicle_cmd_gate.param.yaml The last limits before the vehicle interface.

docs.title: 3. Overlay Workspace
docs.text:
Put ROS packages in overlay_ws/src and build them in the universe-common-devel image from the same build as your runtime images. A release pins that image next to its runtime images, so the CLI builds with the right one:

openadkit build [--ros-distro humble]   # in the kit: its overlay_ws
openadkit build PATH                    # any workspace, with the pins of the kit around it
openadkit build -- --packages-select my_pkg                # arguments after -- go to colcon build
openadkit build -- --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug   # Release unless you set another

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
• Packages build incrementally: a second build compiles only what changed.
  • The CLI records the image and distro in install/.openadkit-overlay.json. After a base upgrade or a distro change, validate and run warn until you rebuild, and that rebuild starts from a clean build/ and install/, since CMake caches record the paths they were configured with.
  • --install-base and --build-base stay fixed: the services source install/ where they mount the workspace.
  • A source checkout pins no devel image: set DEVEL_IMAGE to the matching universe-common-devel digest from the build's metadata.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
The workspace belongs to the kit: the one overlay_ws at the kit root serves every deployment of the kit, since they all extend one base and its images. Every Autoware service mounts it, and the entrypoint hook sources overlay_ws/install/local_setup.bash on top of Autoware, so its packages are visible in every service. Whether your code runs depends on what starts it:

  • A changed copy of an Autoware package shadows the image's own. It runs where Autoware already launches that package, with nothing more to configure; Autoware packages that link against its library keep the copy they were built with.
  • A new node runs only where something starts it: an extra service (as the example kit's acme-probe), a launch file you override under config/autoware, or by hand with openadkit shell <service> ros2 run <package> <node>.

docs.title: Without a Kit
docs.text:
To try a workspace with a reference deployment, without writing a kit, mount it with --ws:

openadkit build ~/my_ws
openadkit run planning-simulation --ws ~/my_ws

--ws is for a deployment without a workspace of its own; on a kit that has one it is an error rather than a second layer.

docs.title: ABI
docs.text: The devel and runtime images install ROS packages from the same ROS snapshot, so an overlay built in the devel image links the ROS versions the runtime image ships. A dependency you add must also exist in the runtime image; the overlay cannot install packages. The example kit's C++ node links diagnostic_updater deliberately to test this devel/runtime boundary, then publishes /acme/probe.

docs.title: 4. Extra Services
docs.text:
Include the base's Compose file through OPENADKIT_BASE_DEPLOYMENT, then define your services under services:. Keep communicating ROS services on the base ROS domain and middleware.

An extra Open AD Kit runtime service loads the kit workspace by mounting ${OPENADKIT_OVERLAY_WS} at /openadkit/overlay_ws:ro, as the example kit's acme-probe does. It needs no image of its own: a runtime image and the workspace are enough. Build your own image only for what the runtime images lack, such as a system package or a non-ROS application, and declare it as an external image (point 5).

To replace one side of a base that runs as split-host nodes, include only the other side's service layer instead of the base's Compose file. For example, a kit that brings its own simulator to carla-simulation includes ${OPENADKIT_BASE_DEPLOYMENT}/services.autoware.yaml: no service in it depends on a CARLA service. The base's resetServices that the kit's services leave out are skipped; the kit's own must exist.

docs.title: 5. Image Replacement
docs.text:
Declare the images your kit uses but does not build in its externalImages, each with either one digest-pinned ref or a distros map of digest-pinned references. A name matching a component image variable replaces that component; other names supply images for new services. Use ${NAME:?} in Compose to require the declared reference.

A replaced base image needs your own runtime evidence: pinning alone does not prove that it honors the entrypoint, launch or parameter interfaces.

docs.title: Validation and Evidence
docs.text:
openadkit validate renders the deployment and checks its manifest (and, with --data, its data). It does not pull images or prove that the runtime works; run reports overrides without a counterpart (see Config Overrides).

Your kit's acceptance checks run where CI runs its own:

  • Readiness: give a service of your own a Compose healthcheck. run waits until it passes. The example kit's acme-probe service runs checks/example_kit.py, which checks the fresh /acme/probe publication of its C++ package and its parameters.
  • End to end: the base's verify step runs on top of your layer with openadkit run --verify. To check something else, name your own in deployment.json: {"verify": {"service": "<service>", "command": [...]}} runs the command in that running service, and without command the step waits for the service to exit and takes its exit code.

The example kit is what openadkit new makes, with a fixture that uses every extension point on top. Its evidence cells run both checks on Humble and Jazzy, each with a workspace built against the matching devel digest, and every release needs them to pass. They show that the extension points work on that build; they do not verify your kit.

A base deployment's CI exemption stays with the kit; an exemption is not runtime evidence. The evidence workflow does not yet accept external kits.

docs.title: Upgrade Without Losing Your Work
docs.text: Install the new base next to the old version, update extends, rebuild your workspace against its devel digest, then validate and run your acceptance checks. Your repository, host settings, downloaded data and output directories are outside the base release, and openadkit upgrade does not change a kit's extends. See Configuration and Downloaded Data.

docs.title: Supported Platforms
docs.text:
Deployments run on Ubuntu with Docker Compose, for development and simulation. Platforms are edge targets on automotive operating systems such as AutoSD.

Open AD Kit is the first SOAFEE blueprint, co-developed with SOAFEE and the eSync Alliance; DENSO's AVP blueprint and Red Hat's AutoSD blueprint build on it.

  • AutoSD — the upstream preview of Red Hat In-Vehicle OS: Quadlet units for Podman and systemd, generated from Compose (experimental)
  • Hardware — host requirements and boards

docs.title: Support Matrix
docs.text:
A supported path is built and shipped by every release and covered by Compatibility; the notes say where CI evidence does not reach it. An experimental one works but may change in a minor release. An unsupported one is not built or tested here.

A path that fails its build or validation gate is dropped or marked here, not documented as if it worked. Host requirements and boards are on the Hardware page.

Path Tier Notes Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 + Docker Compose deployments Supported Compose validated in CI; CARLA Simulation runs on 22.04 only Component images, amd64 + arm64 Supported Built and scanned for both; the evidence cells run on amd64. sensing-perception-cuda and planning-cuda are amd64-only; only the amd64 simulator carries the CARLA client Jazzy images Supported A release needs the Humble and the Jazzy evidence cells to pass; Humble is the default CARLA Simulation Supported Humble, amd64, NVIDIA GPU; exempt from CI evidence, checked by hand AutoSD with Podman and Quadlet Experimental Component images, generated from Compose; Planning Simulation only EWAOL Unsupported Arm's Yocto framework and the original SOAFEE reference implementation; no assets in this repository

Other Linux distributions may work but are not tested.

docs.title: AutoSD
docs.text:
Experimental

Running Open AD Kit on AutoSD with Podman and Quadlet may change in a minor release. See Compatibility.

AutoSD (Automotive Stream Distribution) is the public, in-development preview of Red Hat In-Vehicle OS. It is built on CentOS Stream with an automotive kernel and provides:

  • Mixed criticality: safety-critical containers in the root partition, non-critical ones in an isolated QM partition
  • Atomic updates: immutable OSTree images with A/B updates and rollback
  • Real-time kernel for deterministic scheduling
  • Container-native runtime: Podman, Quadlet (systemd container units), and BlueChi orchestration, with no Docker daemon

docs.title: Generate a Deployment
docs.text:
Compose stays the single source. openadkit config prints a deployment's resolved Compose model, and platforms/autosd/quadlet.py translates it:

openadkit fetch planning-simulation
openadkit config planning-simulation \
  | python3 platforms/autosd/quadlet.py --output out --without visualizer \
      --root-password-hash "$(openssl passwd -6 password)"

Use the openadkit of an installed release and platforms/autosd from the same tag: the release's CLI puts the image digests in the model, so the result is pinned. A source checkout names the tags of a local build instead. Kits work the same way, such as openadkit config ./my-kit.

Output Contents out/rootfs/etc/containers/systemd/ A Quadlet unit per service, named after its container out/rootfs/usr/share/openadkit/ The bind-mounted files and data, by mount target out/image.aib.yml Automotive Image Builder manifest that embeds the images and rootfs/; written only with --root-password-hash, since an image has no default password

A Compose field the script does not translate stops it instead of being dropped. It covers what Planning Simulation uses; writable mounts, for example, have no translation yet.

The units run as root with the deployment's host networking. They use the component images, and mapping them onto AutoSD's root and QM partitions is not done yet.

Evidence scope

Evidence runs these units under Podman and systemd on Ubuntu 24.04 and drives the ego to its goal. CI does not build or boot the image below. An image built from these units was driven once by hand: it booted in QEMU with SELinux enforcing and no outside network, and the ego arrived at its goal.

docs.title: Run on a Podman Host
docs.text:
The tree is what an image would contain, so a host with Podman 4.9 or newer, catatonit and systemd can run it:

sudo cp -a out/rootfs/. /
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl start autoware-api autoware-control autoware-perception-simulation \
  autoware-planning autoware-simulator autoware-system autoware-vehicle
systemctl status 'autoware-*'
journalctl -u autoware-control -f

Quadlet registers each .container file as a .service unit. The units pull their images on first start, which takes a while.

docs.title: Build an Image
docs.text:
You need Podman and QEMU; the runner does not work with Docker. Download the Automotive Image Builder runner and build its container:

curl -fL -o auto-image-builder.sh \
  "https://gitlab.com/CentOS/automotive/src/automotive-image-builder/-/raw/main/auto-image-builder.sh?ref_type=heads"
chmod +x auto-image-builder.sh
sudo bash ./auto-image-builder.sh build-builder --distro autosd10-sig

Build the image from the directory you generated out in, because the manifest names its large files by path. /var/tmp goes on disk because the runner's own is in memory and too small for this image. The arguments are the manifest, the container image name, and the disk image to write:

sudo mkdir -p /var/tmp/aib-work
sudo AIB_PODMAN_OPTIONS="-v /var/tmp/aib-work:/var/tmp" bash ./auto-image-builder.sh build \
  --distro autosd10-sig \
  --target qemu \
  --define-file platforms/autosd/vars.yml \
  out/image.aib.yml \
  localhost/openadkit:latest \
  disk.qcow2
sudo chown "$(logname)" disk.qcow2

To run Automotive Image Builder directly instead, use an RPM-based host (Fedora, CentOS, or RHEL) with Automotive Image Builder, OSBuild, and QEMU installed.

docs.title: Run the Image
docs.text:
With Automotive Image Builder's runner, air, installed:

air disk.qcow2

Or with QEMU directly:

/usr/bin/qemu-system-x86_64 \
  -drive file=/usr/share/OVMF/OVMF_CODE.fd,if=pflash,format=raw,unit=0,readonly=on \
  -drive file=/usr/share/OVMF/OVMF_VARS.fd,if=pflash,format=raw,unit=1,snapshot=on,readonly=off \
  -smp 20 \
  -nographic \
  -enable-kvm \
  -m 16384 \
  -machine q35 \
  -cpu host \
  -device virtio-net-pci,netdev=n0,mac=FE:00:e2:0d:ba:4d \
  -netdev user,id=n0,net=10.0.2.0/24,hostfwd=tcp::2222-:22 \
  -drive file=disk.qcow2,index=0,media=disk,format=qcow2,if=virtio,id=rootdisk,snapshot=off

-m 16384 (16 GB) is the minimum for the Autoware stack; use -m 32768 for heavier workloads. -m 2G is enough only to boot and explore the OS. Log in as root with the password you hashed in Generate a Deployment, here password, which is for this demo only.

docs.text: What a host needs to run Open AD Kit, and the boards with their own support.

docs.title: Host Requirements
docs.text:
For deployments, simulation and development:

Resource Minimum Recommended CPU 8 cores 16 cores RAM 16 GB 32 GB GPU None NVIDIA with 2 GB+ VRAM for Planning Simulation's GPU mode, 4 GB+ for Logging Simulation's; 16 GB for CARLA Simulation Storage 50 GB 100 GB+ SSD

Images are published for amd64 and arm64. The GPU modes and CARLA Simulation are amd64-only: the CUDA images do not fall back to CPU, so hosts without an NVIDIA GPU, and all arm64 hosts, run the CPU images.

On a host below the recommended size Autoware may not keep up in real time; Scenario Simulation can then run slower than real time with GLOBAL_REAL_TIME_FACTOR.

Board Architecture Support R-Car X5H arm64 AutoSD 10 image in openadkit-rcar-x5h, its own repository; board tests are manual

No board is part of the release evidence: the evidence cells run on hosted amd64 runners, and native arm64 cells are on the roadmap.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text:
v2.0.0 is not published yet

Until the first stable release there is no release bundle to install. A source checkout runs images you build yourself; see Build from Source.

GitHub Releases is the canonical source for published versions, release notes and provenance metadata. Each stable release publishes:

  • a versionless openadkit installer
  • the versioned openadkit-vX.Y.Z.tar.gz bundle: the CLI and the deployments
  • release-plan.json and release-metadata.json: the pinned Autoware release, ROS 2 distros, image tags and digests, the BOM, the passing evidence summary and the CI exemptions
  • build provenance for the installer, bundle, plan and metadata

The release notes open with the highlights and the install command, list the merged pull requests by type, and summarize the evidence. An installed release moves to the latest stable version with openadkit upgrade.

  • Container Images & Versioning — image tags and what to pin
  • Compatibility — what a version number promises
  • Evidence Policy — what a build must pass to be released
  • Verify a Release — check the files before you run them
  • Roadmap — planned work, in priority order

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
Open AD Kit follows Semantic Versioning from v2.0.0. This page lists what that promise covers. Within one major version:

  • A patch release (v2.0.1) fixes bugs and keeps every item below working.
  • A minor release (v2.1.0) adds features and may move to a newer Autoware release. It keeps every item below working. JSON output and manifests can gain new fields, which readers should ignore.
  • A major release (v3.0.0) is the only one that removes or changes an item below. Its release notes list each change under Breaking changes.

Experimental features and what is not covered can change in any release.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
• The commands and options in openadkit --help and openadkit <command> --help.
  • Exit status: Status Meaning 0 Success 1 Failure, with an error: line on stderr 2 Usage error, such as a missing deployment name 130 Interrupted

    run --verify exits with the verify step's own status.

  • Machine-readable output: list --json, version --json, validate --json and each run's results/run.json. Each carries schemaVersion.

docs.title: Manifests
docs.text: • The kit manifest openadkit.json and the deployment manifest deployment.json at schemaVersion: 2: their fields and what they mean. A deployment is named by its key in the kit manifest.

docs.title: Kits
docs.text:
What a kit made with openadkit new builds on:

  • extends pinning a release, and base naming one of its deployments.
  • The Compose variables OPENADKIT_BASE_ROOT, OPENADKIT_BASE_DEPLOYMENT and OPENADKIT_OVERLAY_WS.
  • Each base deployment's Compose entrypoints, service names, data destination variables (such as MAP_PATH), verify step and the settings listed under Settings and Paths.
  • Config overrides under config/ and the overlay workspace in overlay_ws/, which the images' entrypoint applies and sources on every start.
  • externalImages that replace a component image or add new ones.

See Create a Kit and the Integrator Guide.

docs.title: Settings and Paths
docs.text:
• OPENADKIT_VERBOSE, OPENADKIT_INSTALL_DIR, OPENADKIT_CONFIG_DIR and OPENADKIT_OUTPUT_DIR.
  • The host settings file ~/.config/openadkit/<deployment>.env, and the results and recordings directories under the output directory.
  • These settings of a deployment's settings.env and of the host settings file: the data destination variables, VEHICLE_MODEL, SENSOR_MODEL, VEHICLE_ID, CYCLONEDDS_NETWORK_INTERFACE, and the visualizer's REMOTE_DISPLAY, REMOTE_PASSWORD, RVIZ_CONFIG, RVIZ_GPU, WEBSOCKIFY_BIND, NOVNC_CERT and NOVNC_KEY.

See CLI & Maintenance.

docs.title: Images
docs.text:
• Component image names and the tag scheme: release tags, latest aliases and the devel image a kit builds its overlay in. See Container Images & Versioning.
  • The image labels org.opencontainers.image.autoware-base-version and org.opencontainers.image.ros-snapshot.
  • The Autoware packages that the catalog deployments run and that each image's launch files in Components need, with RViz plugins in the visualizer image only. They change only with the pinned Autoware release: when Autoware removes a package, the minor release that moves to that Autoware release says so. An image may lose any other package in a minor release, whose notes list it.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text:
• The versionless installer and its install, upgrade, uninstall and setup commands.
  • The openadkit-vX.Y.Z.tar.gz bundle, and the fields of release-metadata.json and release-plan.json.

docs.title: Experimental
docs.text:
These work and are tested where the docs say so, but may change in a minor release:

  • Split-host nodes: --node, nodes in deployment.json and the Zenoh bridge. See Split-host Simulation.
  • AutoSD with Podman and Quadlet: platforms/autosd/ and the units it generates. See AutoSD.
  • The Diffusion Planner: planning-simulation --gpu. With Autoware 2.0.0 its verify step fails on the sample route. See Planning Simulation.

docs.title: Not Covered
docs.text:
• Human-readable output: messages, tables and their wording.
  • The output of openadkit config, which is Docker Compose's resolved model.
  • The CI workflows and everything under .github/.
  • The other settings in settings.env. Most are arguments of Autoware's launch files and follow the pinned Autoware release; READINESS_CHECKS holds the arguments of the readiness check.
  • Environment variables, files and image internals that this page does not list.

docs.title: Container Images & Versioning
docs.text: Open AD Kit publishes images to the GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/openadkit). This page is the reference for image tags, versions, and what "supported" means.

docs.title: Tag Reference
docs.text:
A release promotes an existing CI build instead of rebuilding it, so the images tested in CI are the images that ship.

Tag Example Created Moves? Release planning-humble-v2.0.0 Every release No Latest alias planning-humble Stable releases Yes Pre-release planning-humble-v2.0.0-rc.1 Pre-releases No CI build planning-humble-123456789-1 Every CI build (<run_id>-<run_attempt>) No

Pre-releases never move the latest aliases. No alias leaves out the distro, so an image never switches ROS distro under the same tag.

Examples use Humble, the default distro. Jazzy images use the same patterns with -jazzy (for example planning-jazzy). sensing-perception-cuda and planning-cuda are amd64-only, and only the amd64 simulator carries the CARLA client.

docs.title: Choosing a Tag
docs.text:
• Reproducible deployments: use a release tag (vX.Y.Z) or a digest.
  • Latest stable for a distro: use <target>-<ros_distro>.
  • Never pin per-architecture tags such as universe-common-amd64-humble: CI moves them with every build of main, and publishes them only for the common images its own builds start from.
  • Source checkout: ./openadkit runs <target>-<arch>-<ros_distro>, the tags of a local build, not published images.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
Open AD Kit versions follow Semantic Versioning on their own, starting at v2.0.0: a backward-incompatible change to the CLI, the manifests or a deployment raises the major version, and a move to a new Autoware release raises at least the minor version. The release notes list what breaks, and Compatibility lists what a major version keeps working.

  • One Autoware release per release. Releases come from main, which pins one Autoware release in .github/autoware.ref. The GitHub Release title pairs the two, Open AD Kit v2.0.1 · Autoware 2.0.0, and so do openadkit install and openadkit version.
  • Pinned inputs. A release also pins the ROS 2 distros and every image digest, and its images carry org.opencontainers.image.autoware-base-version.
  • Backports. A fix that is upstream but not yet in an Autoware release can be backported; the release notes list it, and the Autoware version stays the tag's.
  • Older versions. A release/X.Y branch is created from a release tag only to fix an older version.

docs.title: ROS 2 Distro Support
docs.text:
Distro Status Humble Default Jazzy Supported

A release bundle pins images for both distros; choose one with --ros-distro. A release needs the evidence cells of both distros to pass its gate, and a distro is supported only while it is supported upstream. Changing the default takes a reviewed manifest change and passing evidence; a release never falls back to another distro by itself. Evidence runs on amd64, so an image build alone does not prove runtime behavior on arm64.

docs.title: ROS Package Snapshot
docs.text:
Every image installs its ROS packages from one dated ROS snapshot: the one the upstream Autoware images of that release were built from. Compiled code and runtime therefore use the same ROS versions, and the build fails if they would differ. The release BOM names the snapshot per distro; an image carries it as a label:

docker inspect --format '{{ index .Config.Labels "org.opencontainers.image.ros-snapshot" }}' \
  ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/openadkit:planning-humble

The snapshot changes only with the upstream Autoware release. Ubuntu packages are not pinned, so security updates keep flowing into new builds.

docs.title: What "Supported" Means
docs.text:
• Releases: the latest stable release is supported. Fixes, including CVE remediation, ship in a new release; older releases are not patched.
  • Platforms: a path is supported, experimental or unsupported. See Supported Platforms.
  • No certification claims: Open AD Kit makes no safety-certification, functional-safety or production-readiness claim.

Community help and version coverage are described in SUPPORT.md; report security vulnerabilities through the private reporting policy.

Maintainers: see the Release Process.

docs.title: Evidence Policy
docs.text: A release promotes an existing build. It does not rebuild images or relax its tests: stable releases and release candidates both require a successful evidence run that passed every cell for the promoted build.

docs.title: What the Gate Checks
docs.text:
Before creating a tag, release validation looks for an evidence-summary-<build_tag> artifact and accepts it only when:

  1. The run succeeded: it is a completed, successful run of .github/workflows/evidence.yaml on the branch that built the release.
  2. It tested this build: the summary names the promoted build tag, and it tested the build's own commit, not another commit against its images.
  3. Every cell passed: the summary result is PASSED. A cell passes only when every level it runs passes, and a missing expected cell fails the run.

A passing rerun may supersede a failed run; a failed run never counts. There is no release bypass input. The release also requires the latest full scan of the build to pass.

docs.title: Cells and Levels
docs.text:
Evidence cells are enumerated from the deployment manifests, one per ROS distro and topology:

Deployment Distros Topologies Planning Simulation Humble, Jazzy Single host; also under Podman and systemd with the AutoSD units Scenario Simulation Humble, Jazzy Single host; two isolated nodes on one host Safety Island Simulation Humble, Jazzy Single host, with the pinned Safety Island release over domain_bridge example-kit Humble, Jazzy Single host: a kit made with openadkit new on Planning Simulation, plus a fixture that uses every extension point

Each cell runs these levels on a fresh stack, started with openadkit run --no-visualizer:

  • L0: manifests and Compose configuration validate.
  • L1: openadkit run returns: the deployment's healthchecks pass, so its ROS interfaces are present and its topics publish.
  • L2: the deployment's verify step passes (openadkit run --verify): the Planning Simulation ego arrives at its goal, or the scenarios pass, plus the split-node checks.
  • L3: the example kit only: the development loop on the running stack. Its C++ package changes, openadkit build builds it, openadkit restart from another directory recreates the services, and the stack publishes the change.

The example kit gates a release like every other cell: it shows that each kit extension point works on the build. It does not verify integrators' own kits.

The workflow retries a failed cell once. A cell that still fails fails the run and blocks the release.

docs.title: What Evidence Does Not Cover
docs.text:
• Other platforms. Every cell runs on a hosted linux/amd64 runner. Images are also built and scanned for arm64, but that is not arm64 runtime evidence, nor two-machine LAN, GPU, HIL or vehicle evidence.
  • GPU modes. Planning Simulation's cells run its CPU mode. Its GPU mode (--gpu, the Diffusion Planner on planning-cuda) validates in CI (L0) and is checked by hand on a GPU host.
  • Real-time behavior. A 4-vCPU hosted runner cannot run Autoware in real time: the ego drives late, and the bundled samples take about three times as long as on a 16-vCPU host. The Scenario Simulation cells therefore run at half speed (GLOBAL_REAL_TIME_FACTOR=0.5, with GLOBAL_TIMEOUT=400 wall-clock seconds) through the cell's host settings file, so they test the scenarios rather than the runner's size.

docs.title: CI Exemptions
docs.text:
CARLA Simulation requires a GPU, and Logging Simulation has no hosted evidence cell yet. Their deployment manifests carry a reasoned evidence.exempt entry. They remain in the bundle, are listed in the release metadata and notes, and the CLI warns when they run. An exemption is not runtime evidence.

Adding an exemption is a reviewed source change, not a release-time override. Do not use it to hide a known failure in a normally tested cell.

docs.title: Autoware and ROS Distro Decisions
docs.text:
Every release, stable or candidate, is a build of main (or of a release/X.Y branch that fixes an older line) on the Autoware release tag in .github/autoware.ref. The release records that Autoware version; the build's autoware-lock.repos, resolved SHA and upstream image digests record the input.

  • Autoware: pin the latest stable Autoware release at the release cut. If it has a blocking issue, keep the previous verified pin and explain the exception, date and follow-up in the release notes. A fix that is already upstream can be backported instead.
  • ROS distro: defaultRosDistro in the promoted openadkit.json selects the default, and the evidence cells of every declared distro must pass. The gate never switches from Humble to Jazzy or drops a failing distro by itself: to change the supported distros, update the manifests in a reviewed change and build and test that revision.

docs.title: Metadata and Verification Report
docs.text:
release-plan.json seals the selected evidence summary (result, build, commit, run URL and cells) before packaging. release-metadata.json includes that same evidence, the BOM and the CI exemptions. The bundle, installer, plan and metadata receive build provenance from the release workflow.

The verification table in the release notes shows the passing-cell count, readiness time, arrival time and peak memory of that build. A release never searches older runs or releases; its notes depend only on the release plan. Missing metrics are shown as -, never replaced with zeroes.

See Verify a Release to check a release yourself, and the Evidence Workflow for how the cells run.

docs.title: Verify a Release
docs.text: Verify downloaded files before executing the installer. The full check needs a recent GitHub CLI with gh attestation, and jq; releases before v2.0.0 may lack these attestations and metadata fields.

docs.title: Provenance and Checksums
docs.text:
Replace the example version with the release you intend to use:

set -euo pipefail
VERSION=v2.0.0
BRANCH=main  # or the release/X.Y branch that released it
REPO=autowarefoundation/openadkit
gh release download "$VERSION" --repo "$REPO" \
  --pattern openadkit --pattern "openadkit-$VERSION.tar.gz" \
  --pattern release-plan.json --pattern release-metadata.json

for asset in openadkit "openadkit-$VERSION.tar.gz" release-plan.json release-metadata.json; do
  gh attestation verify "$asset" --repo "$REPO" \
    --signer-workflow "$REPO/.github/workflows/release.yaml" \
    --source-ref "refs/heads/$BRANCH" --deny-self-hosted-runners
done

The default predicate verifies SLSA build provenance. Provenance binds the bytes to the release workflow; it does not establish that runtime tests passed.

Cross-check the plan and bundle hashes recorded in the verified metadata:

printf '%s  %s\n' "$(jq -r '.release_plan_sha256' release-metadata.json)" release-plan.json \
  | sha256sum --check
jq -r '.bundles[] | .sha256 + "  " + .name' release-metadata.json \
  | sha256sum --check

Review .release, .releaseContext and .evidence in the plan: the requested version, promoted commit, default distro, passing cells and CI exemptions. The metadata's .evidence must match the plan's .evidence exactly, and its url links the evidence run the release gate accepted.

After verification, install with the downloaded openadkit or follow the Quickstart. Evidence is bounded to the tested cells; it is not a vehicle-safety or security certification.

docs.title: Checksum Only
docs.text:
Without the GitHub CLI you can still check the bundle against the release metadata. This proves the bundle is the one the release names, not where it was built:

VERSION=$(curl -fsSL \
  https://api.github.com/repos/autowarefoundation/openadkit/releases/latest \
  | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["tag_name"])')
curl -fLO "https://github.com/autowarefoundation/openadkit/releases/download/${VERSION}/openadkit-${VERSION}.tar.gz"
curl -fLO "https://github.com/autowarefoundation/openadkit/releases/download/${VERSION}/release-metadata.json"
EXPECTED=$(python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("release-metadata.json"))["bundles"][0]["sha256"])')
printf '%s  %s\n' "$EXPECTED" "openadkit-${VERSION}.tar.gz" | sha256sum --check -
tar -xzf "openadkit-${VERSION}.tar.gz"
cd "openadkit-${VERSION}"

The extracted directory is a complete runtime; run it with ./openadkit. The installer makes this same check before it installs a bundle.
